chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan, should he make them up separately? He said: There is no harm in separating the making up of the month of Ramadan. The fasting that must not be separated is the expiation for Dhihar, the expiation for blood (diyah), and the expiation for an oath.
ai.seo_question: Can missed Ramadan fasts be made up on separate days or must they be consecutive?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling qada' (make-up) fasts, distinguishing them from kaffarah (expiation) which mandates consecutive fasting. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the strict continuity required for expiatory acts does not apply to the general obligation of making up missed Ramadan fasts. It provides practical ease for believers who may be unable to fast consecutively due to health or other valid reasons.
